{"url": "https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all%3AHow+do+early+stochastic+interaction+protocols+in+MARL+environments+structurally+constrain+long-term+emergent+preference+persistence+during+non-stationary+training%3F&max_results=4", "scope": "paper abstracts; preprints, peer-review status not verified", "excerpt": "title: Adaptive Calibration in Non-Stationary Environments
id: http://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11490v2
published: 2026-05-12T04:06:40Z
summary: Making calibrated online predictions is a central challenge in modern AI systems. Much of the existing literature focuses on fully adversarial environments where outcomes may be arbitrary, leading to conservative algorithms that can perform suboptimally in more benign settings, such as when outcomes are nearly stationary. This gap raises a natural question: can we design online prediction algorithms whose calibration error automatically adapts to the degree of non-stationarity in the environment, smoothly interpolating between i.i.d. and adversarial regimes? We answer this question in the affirmative and develop a suite of algorithms that achieve adaptive calibration guarantees under multiple calibration measures. Specifically, with $T$ being the number of rounds, $K$ being the unknown number of i.i.d. segments of the environment, and $C\in[0,T]$ being another unknown non-stationary measure defined as the minimal $\ell_1$ deviation of the mean outcomes, our algorithms attain $\widetilde{O}(\min\{\sqrt{T}+(TC)^{\frac{1}{3}}, \sqrt{KT}\})$ for $\ell_1$ calibration error and $\widetilde{O}(\min\{(1+C)^{\frac{1}{3}}, K\})$ for both $\ell_2$ and pseudo KL calibration error. These bounds match the optimal rates in the stationary case ($C=0$ and $K=1$) and recover known guarantees in the fully adversarial regime ($C, K=Ω(T)$). Our approach builds on and extends prior work [Hu et al., 2026, Luo et al., 2025], introducing an epoch-based scheduling together with a novel non-uniform partition of the prediction space that allocates finer resolution near the underlying ground truth.

Dans le contexte de l'émergence de protocole, les nœuds du réseau échangent des messages de contrôle pour coordonner la livraison de données à travers le réseau, le tout sans accord préalable sur la signification de ces messages. Cette approche peut être considérée comme une technique combinée de signalisation et d'optimisation de réseau. L'émergence de protocole offre la possibilité de minimiser les surcharges de signalisation, particulièrement adaptée aux scénarios de communication massive de type machine (MMTC), et facilite la création de protocoles personnalisés adaptés à des applications spécifiques. Cette adaptabilité est particulièrement bénéfique dans des environnements relativement stables, tels que des installations industrielles intérieures. Pour commencer, nous présentons les concepts fondamentaux de l'émergence de protocole en introduisant un cadre. Ce cadre décrit des méthodes pour évaluer les performances des protocoles, caractériser les protocoles, coordonner entre les nœuds et interpréter les messages échangés. Nous analysons ce cadre dans le contexte d'un problème d'accès multiple entrelacé. Dans la partie suivante de ce travail, nous évaluons les performances de l'émergence de protocole dans un scénario impliquant une allocation de ressources contiguë. Non-stationary environments are composed of several different stationary components (i.e., sub-environments or contexts). Therefore, algorithms that accept this assumption are incapable of learning within non-stationary environments. Reinforcement Learning - Context Detection (RL-CD) da Silva et al. (2016) method allows agents to learn the environment, detect context change points, and learn the partial model of the context without previous knowledge of the environment. RL-CD is a single-agent algorithm and it has shortcomings in learning within a multi-agent environment. In this work, we introduce a new method called Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning - Context Detection (MARL-CD), which can both detect context change points and enable agents to learn within non-stationary environments with multi-agent settings. This approach is based on RL-CD and works more effectively in terms of detecting context changes caused by agents and changes caused by the environment’s dynamics. It detects not only the change points originating from the environment, but also the change points created by the agents.
